content:
Maria: Heads-up — after the kernel upgrade (6.2.18 -> 6.3.0) on eu-west-gpu1 yesterday we saw an uptick in Xid67 and ECC correctable counts on a subset of cards.
Raj: Numbers? which clusters/racks?
Maria: Rough: baseline ~2 Xid/day per cluster -> now ~8-10 on affected racks. Affected cards are mostly in rack euw-gpu-12 and euw-gpu-15.
Taylor: Did firmware/driver also change or just kernel?
Maria: Driver stayed at 550.04. Firmware same. Kernel change only.
Sam: If kernel is culprit we should gate the next rollout. Propose canary + thermal/fan profile tweak before wider roll.
Raj: Agreed. Suggest canary on 3 heterogeneous racks (mix of A100 40GB and A10G) for 48h with synthetic load.
Taylor: Also try raising the thermal trip threshold fallback by 5C for the canary hosts, and enable more aggressive fan curve. That reduced transient ECC in past incidents.
Maria: I've got a quick grep that collected recent errors — dropping snippet here:
```
[2026-03-16T02:14:22Z] gpu0: Xid 67, reason: MMU_FAULT
[2026-03-16T02:14:25Z] gpu0: ECC correctable: 124 -> 130
[2026-03-16T02:22:03Z] gpu1: Xid 67, reason: MMU_FAULT
[2026-03-16T03:01:11Z] gpu3: ECC correctable: 3 -> 7
```
Sam: Thanks. Can we also run the nvml health-export script nightly and upload to S3 for long-term comparison?
Ingrid: I'll open a vendor ticket for the serials in the affected racks and ask if kernel 6.3.0 exposes any known MMU reg timing issues.
canary-bot: Canary job started on racks: euw-gpu-03, euw-gpu-12, euw-gpu-21 at 2125550100. Config: kernel=6.3.0, fan-curve=+10% pwm, thermal-fallback=+5C.
Raj: Good. Add a watch to alert on >3 Xid events per card/hour during canary. Ops-bot please create alert.
ops-bot: alert created: gpu.xid.rate_threshold (3/hr) -> PagerDuty escalation policy infra-oncall.
Taylor: If canary looks clean after 24h then we can try the kernel on one additional region with the same protective profile. If not, rollback to 6.2.18 and run bisect.
Maria: Early canary update (8h): euw-gpu-12 had 2 Xid events (both during synthetic memory stress), euw-gpu-03 had 0, euw-gpu-21 had 1.
Sam: that's lower than prod spike but still nonzero. We should capture perf/telemetry around the Xid timestamps (PCIe link stats + mem clk).
Ingrid: Extracted the card serials and sent to vendor. Also included core dumps.
Raj: Ops: let's prepare drain+replace playbook for cards that exceed 10 Xid in 24h or show rising ECC uncorrectables. Template:
```
- mark node cordoned
- migrate pods with gpu requests
- run burnin 6h (mem+tf) under driver 550.04
- if fails -> RMA / replace
```
Taylor: Add note: if burnin shows intermittent Xid but ECC remains increasing, escalate to hw replacement even if burnin passes sometimes. Flaky cards hide.
Maria: For rollout gating: require canary 48h with <=1 Xid/card/day and fan-curve applied, otherwise rollback. Also add automated thermal rollback on nodes that cross 85C for more than 30s.
canary-bot: Canary 24h summary: euw-gpu-03: 0 Xid, euw-gpu-12: 4 Xid, euw-gpu-21: 1 Xid. Average temp delta +3C vs baseline.
Sam: euw-gpu-12 is borderline. Can we isolate which physical cards? Maria please map instance->pci-id->serial.
Maria: Doing that now, will paste mapping in follow-up thread.
Ingrid: Vendor responded: they haven't flagged 6.3.0 but asked for logs and asked whether pci lane retrains occurred. Requested pcie logs.
Raj: Next steps checklist:
- Finish mapping and attach to vendor ticket (Ingrid)
- Continue canary to 48h unless alert trips (Maria)
- Prepare rollback package and automation (Taylor)
- Draft replacement playbook and ordering lead times (Sam)
- Keep oncall informed (ops-bot)
Maria: I'll also re-run canary with a kernel config that disables a new MMU prefetch flag (if build permits) as a cheaper test before full rollback.
Taylor: +1. If that reproves clean we can upstream a kernel patch.
Raj: Thanks all. Ping here with the 48h canary summary and RMA status. :thumbsup:
